description: Figure 1 is a horizontal bar chart titled “Number of tasks by language family,” which visually represents the distribution of probing tasks across ten distinct language families. The vertical axis lists the language families in descending order of task count: IE-Slavic, IE-Romance, IE-Germanic, Uralic, IE-Baltic, IE-other, IE-Indic, Semitic, Turkic, and Basque. Each family is associated with a uniquely colored horizontal bar extending to the right, with its length proportional to the number of tasks. The horizontal axis, labeled “# tasks,” is scaled from 0 to 80 in increments of 10. IE-Slavic has the longest bar, indicating approximately 78 tasks, followed by IE-Romance at about 48 tasks and IE-Germanic at roughly 45 tasks. The remaining families show progressively fewer tasks: Uralic (~20), IE-Baltic (~17), IE-other (~15), IE-Indic (~11), Semitic (~9), Turkic (~6), and Basque (~4). The chart uses distinct pastel shades for each bar, with no grouping or stacking, and the bars are sorted in descending order of magnitude to emphasize the disparity in task coverage across language families.
